claims.claim_text: The indexed Louis A Ojibway is Louis Austin O'Jibway.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The CIA-published study uses the expanded name and cites his completed OSS requisition in Entry 224, Box 570.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the uncommon name, matching commissioned-officer chronology, exact box, and direct personnel-file citation.
claims.temporal_assessment: The cited requisition is dated April 3, 1944, immediately before the article's documented OSS arrival on April 27.
claims.match_notes: The article's personnel-file citation supplies a direct archival bridge without exposing the service identifier.

claims.claim_text: Immediately before OSS recruitment in 1944, O'Jibway was athletic director at the Cavalry Replacement Training Center at Fort Riley.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The study places O'Jibway at Fort Riley from his 1942 appointment through his 1944 volunteer recruitment by the OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact personnel-file bridge and distinctive expanded name establish that the chronology belongs to the indexed captain.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly immediate: the Fort Riley discussion runs through 1944 and is followed by his OSS recruitment and April 27 arrival.
claims.match_notes: This is a military assignment, not a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: After his 1941 draft, O'Jibway served in the physical-training unit at First Cavalry Division headquarters.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The study describes his promotion to corporal and assignment to the division headquarters physical-training unit before officer training.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The chronology is part of the same directly bridged biography of the indexed captain.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented before the 1942 Fort Riley appointment and 1944 OSS recruitment.
claims.match_notes: This earlier military role is not marked as the immediate pre-OSS affiliation.

claims.claim_text: O'Jibway studied petroleum engineering at the University of New Mexico from 1939 until his September 1941 draft.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The study cites his UNM transcript and describes two academic years, his major, and the draft at the start of his senior year.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The rare expanded name and personnel-file bridge identify the indexed captain.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the civilian status immediately before Army service, but not employment.
claims.match_notes: UNM is intentionally modeled as student status, not as employer evidence.

sources.locator_override: PDF page 2 and PDF page 16, note 9

claims.claim_text: Before Army service, O'Jibway worked summers as a roughneck in oil fields and steel yards; no employer is named.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The study reports summer roughneck work while explaining how he paid non-scholarship expenses.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The directly bridged biography identifies the same Louis Austin O'Jibway.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented during his prewar education, but not shown to be his last civilian employment.
claims.match_notes: No oil or steel company is inferred, and this occupation-only claim does not enter employer analytics or the oil-company directory.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Leif Oistad is the technical sergeant who served in the 99th Infantry Battalion and OSS NORSO.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The indexed name and private identifier match the Army record; the obituary independently matches rank, unit, OSS group, and wartime chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from an exact nonshared identifier plus multiple independent biographical identifiers.
claims.temporal_assessment: The obituary places the 99th Battalion assignment and OSS recruitment in the 1942-45 wartime sequence.
claims.match_notes: The private identifier is used only for resolution and is not reproduced publicly.

claims.claim_text: OSS recruited Oistad from the 99th Infantry Battalion (Separate) at Camp Hale, where he instructed soldiers in skiing.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The obituary names the Camp Hale battalion and ski-instructor role, then states that OSS recruited him to form NORSO.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact Army identifier, indexed technical-sergeant rank, and obituary chronology establish the person.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly immediate because the source states OSS recruitment from the named Army assignment.
claims.match_notes: This is a military assignment and is excluded from civilian-employer counts.

claims.claim_text: Before Army service, Oistad worked as a deckhand on commercial vessels, including the oil tanker Brasil; no employer is established.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The obituary says he became a deckhand in 1936 and worked on several commercial vessels before his 1942 Army recruitment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact Army identifier and matching service chronology establish the person.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented before Army service, but neither the final pre-service voyage nor an employing company is stated.
claims.match_notes: A vessel described as a Texaco tanker does not establish that Texaco employed Oistad, so he is not added to the oil-company directory.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Takashi Ohta is the OSS civilian employee named in April 1945 overseas travel orders.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A corrected OSS order names Takashi Ohta among civilian employees authorized for overseas temporary duty.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the rare exact name in both the personnel index and a contemporary primary OSS order.
claims.temporal_assessment: The order is dated April 30, 1945 and establishes wartime OSS employment, not the start date.
claims.match_notes: The source supplies an independent OSS-context bridge without inventing a middle name or service number.

claims.claim_text: Ohta was hired as a set designer for the Provincetown Players in 1928.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Woodstock art-history article explicitly states that Ohta was hired for this New York theatre role in 1928.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The rare exact name aligns with the primary OSS order, but the theatre article does not itself mention OSS.
claims.temporal_assessment: Definitely pre-OSS; a long chronology gap prevents treating it as immediate or the last civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: Published with visible qualification and excluded from default high-confidence employer analytics.

claims.claim_text: Later in 1928, Ohta became set designer and scenic director of the Maverick Theatre in West Hurley.

claims.identity_match_assessment: The rare exact name aligns with the primary OSS order, but the theatre article does not itself mention OSS.
claims.temporal_assessment: Definitely pre-OSS; the endpoint and intervening 1930s-40s chronology remain unresolved.
